t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a full deep navy background. Light-weight sans-serif headline top left with a small monospace eyebrow. A single thick limestone-coloured ribbon path snakes left to right across the middle like a route on a map, entering as a fan of streams and leaving as diverging arrows. Seven circular stop nodes with glowing steel-blue rings sit on its peaks and troughs, each with a small fine-line glyph nearby and tiny mono data readouts. Below, seven evenly spaced caption columns with slash-numbered labels for <CONTENT>. Calm, technical, generous space, square corners.
signature_idea: The skid's treatment train is drawn as one continuous water route with seven stops, so the sequence reads like a journey map.
strengths: sequence is instantly legible, one stop per stage with aligned captions
on-brand navy/limestone with a single accent, light headline
maps directly to an animated stepper with hotspots
glyphs give each stage identity without clutter
weaknesses: wavy ribbon is decorative; real skid is not a rollercoaster and wave heights mean nothing
glow rings and soft shading drift toward generic infographic
hover hints are not usable on phones
some glyphs are vague (heat exchanger as wave grid)
brand_fit_why: Navy ground, limestone route, one steel-blue accent, light headline and mono labels fit the brand; the soft glows and wavy decorative route are slightly less precise than the line-art ideal.
